description: We are Zenvyra, a team of six passionate students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We aim to explore Earth's changing systems using NASA data, technology, and creative problem-solving. Through innovation, teamwork, and web development, we hope to make environmental data easier to understand and visualize. Together, we are excited to learn, collaborate, and create meaningful solutions for a better understanding of our planet.
summary:
NASA Data Detectives – Zenvyra: Earth System Trend Detective

Zenvyra is an interactive Earth science exploration platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective."

Inspired by the significance of our pale blue dot, Zenvyra transforms complex NASA Earth observation data into meaningful scientific discoveries. By combining satellite datasets, advanced statistical analysis, and interactive visualizations, it helps uncover environmental patterns and changes across Earth's systems.

Powered by a Python-based backend, Zenvyra analyzes temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation using scientific methods such as OLS regression, Theil-Sen estimation, and Mann-Kendall testing. It presents these insights through interactive 3D Earth visualizations, geographical exploration, climate dashboards, trend analysis, and anomaly detection.
Our vision: Transforming data into discovery, revealing the story of our changing planet, and empowering the next generation of Earth explorers.
details:
ZENVYRA – An Interactive Earth System Trend Explorer

1. Project Overview and Working

ZENVYRA is an interactive Earth science exploration platform that helps users understand how our planet is changing over time. It allows students, researchers, educators, and citizen scientists to explore environmental trends using NASA Earth observation data.

The platform focuses on five important environmental variables: surface temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, aerosol optical depth, and vegetation health (NDVI).

Users can explore different locations using an interactive 3D Earth globe, search for cities, select environmental variables, and examine changes across different years. The system analyses the selected data to identify whether an environmental variable is increasing, decreasing, or showing no clear long-term trend.

It uses statistical methods such as Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Theil–Sen estimation, and the Mann–Kendall test. It also removes seasonal variations to make long-term trends easier to understand.

The results are displayed through graphs, visual indicators, and simple explanations.

The platform connects with NASA Earthdata services and also includes cached and demonstration datasets to support exploration when live data access is unavailable.

2. Key Benefits

  • Makes complex NASA Earth science information easier to access and understand.
  • Helps users identify long-term environmental changes.
  • Provides statistical analysis to distinguish meaningful trends from normal variations.
  • Combines multiple environmental variables in one platform.
  • Uses interactive maps, graphs, and 3D visualizations to improve learning.
  • Supports educational exploration through simple explanations.
  • Provides demonstration datasets and caching for continued exploration when live NASA data is unavailable.

3. Intended Impact

Our main goal is to make Earth science data more accessible, understandable, and useful for everyone.

ZENVYRA encourages people to explore environmental changes, understand climate-related patterns, and become more aware of the connections between different Earth systems.

For example, users can investigate whether rainfall is increasing or decreasing in a region, examine changes in soil moisture, and explore how these patterns relate to other environmental variables.

The project can support environmental education, student research, scientific awareness, and informed discussions about climate and sustainability.

Our long-term vision is to make satellite-based Earth observation data easier for everyone to explore and understand.

4. Technologies and Tools Used

Programming Languages

  • Python
  • JavaScript
  • TypeScript
  • HTML
  • CSS

Frameworks and Libraries

  • React – Builds the user interface.
  • FastAPI – Connects the frontend with the Python backend.
  • Three.js – Creates interactive 3D Earth visualizations.
  • Leaflet – Provides interactive maps.
  • NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas – Handle scientific calculations and data processing.
  • Vite – Supports frontend development and building.

Data and Services

  • NASA Earthdata services
  • NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR)
  • Earthdata authentication through earthaccess

Development Software

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Git and GitHub
  • Web browser

Hardware

A standard computer or laptop was used for development. No specialized hardware was required.

5. Creativity and Innovation

ZENVYRA combines scientific data analysis with an immersive and interactive visual experience.

Instead of presenting users with complicated scientific tables and raw datasets, it allows them to explore Earth through a 3D globe, interactive maps, timelines, and visual trend charts.

One of its key creative features is the combination of multiple statistical techniques. By using OLS, Theil–Sen estimation, and the Mann–Kendall test, the platform provides different perspectives on environmental trends.

Another important feature is converting complex statistical results into simple explanations that beginners can understand.

The platform also includes multilingual support, accessibility features, and visual alternatives for devices with limited graphics capabilities.

6. Key Development Considerations

While developing ZENVYRA, our team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific Reliability: Using established statistical methods to analyse long-term environmental trends.
  • Data Accessibility: Making NASA Earth observation information easier to explore.
  • User Experience: Designing a simple and interactive interface for beginners and experienced users.
  • Performance: Using caching and demonstration datasets to improve accessibility and reduce loading delays.
  • Accessibility: Considering different users, screen readability, and devices with limited graphics capabilities.
  • Security: Including API security measures, request validation, and rate limiting.
  • Educational Value: Presenting scientific results in simple language so users can understand their meaning.
  • Scalability: Designing the platform to support additional environmental variables and future features.

Conclusion

ZENVYRA transforms Earth science exploration into an interactive learning experience. By combining NASA Earth observation data, statistical analysis, and immersive visualizations, our project aims to help people become Earth System Trend Detectives and better understand the environmental changes happening around our planet.
